In this section we elucidate some of the results obtained previously on closed
immersions of schemes. Recall that a morphism of schemes <MATH_0001>
is defined to be a closed immersion if (a) <MATH_0002> induces a homeomorphism onto
a closed subset of <MATH_0003>, (b) <MATH_0004>
is surjective, and (c) the kernel of <MATH_0005> is locally generated by
sections, see Schemes, Definitions <REF_0001>
and <REF_0002>. It turns
out that, given that <MATH_0006> and <MATH_0007> are schemes, there are many different
ways of characterizing a closed immersion.
